scope: Consolidated selection/navigation checkpoint; not complete-course acceptance

checkpoint.title: Select, navigate and undo
checkpoint.goal: Orbit a perspective scene, select its nearest visible triangle, and undo or redo document edits without losing identity.
checkpoint.trace: canvas coordinates → viewing ray → nearest triangle → object identity → reversible scene snapshot
checkpoint.question: Why must undo preserve both an object's ID and the highest identity already issued?
checkpoint.answer: Restored objects keep references meaningful. Preserving the highest issued identity prevents a new branch from assigning an old identity to a different object.
checkpoint.story: One camera supplies both the rendered projection and the picking ray. History keeps document snapshots independently of the camera and GPU resources.
checkpoint.result: The visible selected triangle is yellow. Orbit changes the view; delete exposes the triangle behind it; undo restores the original identity and shared mesh.
checkpoint.experiment: Delete the nearer triangle, undo, then make a different edit. Predict the selected object and whether redo still has a branch.
checkpoint.production: The maintained viewer also keeps camera motion separate from source geometry. Its current camera adds framed viewports, units, fitting and anchored projection; cumulative production parity remains unfinished.
checkpoint.browser_status: Orbit moves the eye around a fixed target.
checkpoint.image_result: Look at the overlap: the pink triangle now covers the centre while the cyan triangle sits above it. The helper sets the camera to Isometric and checks the centre pixel against picking. This image shows the camera pose, not a mouse gesture.

edits.why: Declare the kernel math dependency used by projection and ray intersection.
Declare the camera, picking and history modules.
Keep quaternion navigation, perspective projection and unprojection together.
Choose the nearest triangle intersecting the clipped viewing ray.
Restore snapshots without recycling an object identity.
Retain shared-mesh snapshots and bounded undo/redo branches.
Upload selection colour while preserving source mesh data.
Rebuild displayed meshes when document or selection changes.
Route canvas input, navigation and reversible document commands.
